posts.description: After Lead Poisoning Symptoms Dismissed by PTSD Diagnosis, It Results in Brain Inflammation, Fatigue, Muscle Weakness, Digestion Issues & Chronic Pain (2024) A cautionary tale for anyone with unexplained symptoms By Jennifer S. Norris, U.S. Air Force Retired I took care of myself my entire life because I knew I had no one to fall back on. I paid attention to my body. I tried to eat well, stay capable, work hard, and make the kind of choices that would let me remain independent. I believed that if I did my part, I could protect my future. Then I got sick while serving in the Air Force. I did not know that the environment around me might be part of the story. I could control what I ate and how hard I worked. I could not control what had been left in the soil, what was moving through groundwater, or whether anyone thought to warn the people serving there. That is why I am writing this. posts.title: Monkey in the Middle: The Hero Trap in the Spencer Newcomer Case on Investigation Discovery’s Fear Thy Neighbor Series (November 5, 2026)
posts.description: The Sneaky Predator at the Barbecue: Why “The Sociopath Next Door” Book Is an Essential Wake-Up Call for Society A manipulator can make you feel like a hero while encouraging you to do something that could destroy your life. Before you confront someone on another person’s behalf, consider whose problem you are being asked to solve—and who will face the consequences. The Spencer Newcomer case deserves another look through that lens. The fatal neighborhood dispute featured in Fear Thy Neighbor’s “Monkey in the Middle” raises questions about escalation, private encouragement, and the accountability of people outside the final confrontation. This episode portrayed a neighbor repeatedly feeding the conflict between David Wintermyer and Spencer Newcomer. On June 10, 2012, Newcomer fatally shot Wintermyer during a confrontation in Springettsbury Township, Pennsylvania. Newcomer maintained that he believed Wintermyer was drawing a gun. posts.description: When Image Matters More Than Truth: How Toxic People Control the Narrative and Create Scapegoats to Avoid Accountability (August 5, 2026) The Tracey Higley disciplinary record was not merely a personnel problem. It was an institutional risk warning. What should responsible municipal leadership do when it learns that a police officer entrusted with the power to detain, arrest and use force has accumulated repeated complaints involving intimidation, judgment, supervision, vulnerable people, professional boundaries and fear of retaliation? That question matters because Rumford was not operating without warning. The disciplinary record published on our website describes a pattern rather than a single bad day. Town Manager Steve Eldridge imposed a demotion to Patrolman I and seven days without pay after describing repeated misconduct despite previous opportunities to improve.
